**Roster is a desktop application that helps teaching assistants manage students across multiple tutorial groups.**

Designed for fast, keyboard-driven use during class, Roster allows TAs to record attendance and short comments, search student records and export attendance to CSV. Keeping student details and attendance together helps TAs identify students who may need additional support.

Roster is designed for NUS teaching assistants who manage multiple tutorial groups from a laptop during class. It is aimed at TAs who are comfortable typing commands and need to update records while teaching, then review those records after class.

Keep each student's details, tutorial group and attendance together instead of maintaining separate spreadsheets. Roster aims to reduce the effort of finding and updating class records, so TAs can focus on teaching and identifying students who may need timely, targeted support.
- **Tutorial groups:** Create separate groups and move between group views without mixing up their student records.
- **Student records:** Add students with their identifying details and tutorial group, and delete records that are no longer needed.
- **Roster views:** List students across all groups or view the students in one tutorial group.
- **Student search:** Find students by complete or partial name, exact matriculation number, tutorial group, or a combination of these filters.
- **Attendance:** Record a student as present or absent for a tutorial session, while keeping unrecorded attendance distinct from confirmed absence.
- **Comments:** Append, replace or clear a short comment for a student.
- **Undo:** Reverse changes during the current application session.
- **CSV export:** Export attendance for all students or a specified tutorial group to a new CSV file.
Participation records and assignment-completion tracking are not implemented. Roster does not cover grading or communicating with students.

This project uses Gradle for **build automation and dependency management**. **We recommend reading [this Gradle tutorial from se-edu/guides](https://se-education.org/guides/tutorials/gradle.html).**
The following commands perform common Gradle tasks.
* **`clean`**: Deletes the files created during the previous build tasks (e.g. files in the `build` folder).
* **`shadowJar`**: Uses the Shadow plugin to create the fat JAR file `build/libs/roster.jar`.
**`runShadow`**: Builds the application as a fat JAR, then runs it.
* **`checkstyleMain`**: Runs the code style check for the main code base.
**`checkstyleTest`**: Runs the code style check for the test code base.
* `./gradlew clean test`: Cleans the project before running all tests
This project uses GitHub Actions for CI. The necessary workflow configuration files are in `.github/workflows`. No further setup is required.
As part of CI, Gradle generates JaCoCo coverage reports from the tests, and CI uploads the coverage data to Codecov. Codecov then provides information about test coverage.

However, because Codecov is known to run into intermittent problems (e.g., report upload fails) due to issues on the Codecov service side, the CI is configured to pass even if the Codecov task failed. Therefore, developers are advised to check the code coverage levels periodically and take corrective actions if the coverage level falls below desired levels.
To enable Codecov for forks of this project, follow the steps given in [this se-edu guide](https://se-education.org/guides/tutorials/codecov.html).

This section describes some noteworthy details on how certain features are implemented.
`editsession grp/GROUP w/WEEK d/DATE` changes only the date of an existing session.
`deletesession grp/GROUP w/WEEK` removes that session and every student's attendance for it.
Their parsers reject missing, repeated and invalid fields before creating the commands.
Each command looks up the session by group/week before changing the model; editing to the same date
is rejected so that it does not add an empty undo step.
`ModelManager` delegates to `AddressBook#setSession` and `AddressBook#removeSession`. Both operate on
the complete student list, independently of the displayed search or group filter. They build replacement
immutable students before changing the session list, retaining names, email, matriculation numbers,
groups, tags, comments and unrelated attendance.
An `Attendance` embeds a complete `Session`, including its date. Updating only `UniqueSessionList`
would therefore leave stale dates in students' stored attendance. Editing replaces each affected
attendance with one referring to the edited session and its original status. Unmarked students stay
unmarked. Deletion removes only attendance with the target group/week identity; it does not infer an absence.
`UniqueSessionList#setSession` disallows changes to the session's group/week identity and preserves
teaching-week display order. Assertions check that edited attendance has the current date and that
deleted sessions leave no attendance records behind.
Both commands use the normal save-and-commit path in `LogicManager`, so they create one undo step each.
Undo restores the session and attendance together. A failed save restores the previous roster without
committing history. Existing observable lists refresh the attendance strips; no storage schema change
or migration is needed. Field completion offers the new commands, their prefixes and registered groups.
**Design choice:** keep group/week as a stable session identity. Rescheduling changes the date while
retaining marks. Moving attendance to a different teaching week or group would be a separate operation
with different meaning; these commands do not silently transfer it.

`StudentMatchesFiltersPredicate` combines the supplied conditions using AND. It delegates name matching

The matcher uses a quoted literal regular expression with Unicode case-insensitive matching, avoiding
context-dependent lowercasing errors such as Greek final sigma. Accents and punctuation remain significant.

The active group is cleared because even a group-filtered search may display only part of a group.

* **Alternative 1 (current choice):** use the session of each student's own group for the given week.
* Pros: works on any displayed list, including search results that mix groups.
* Cons: the same command can update sessions of several groups at once.
* **Alternative 2:** use the session of the active group only.
* Cons: fails, or marks the wrong session, whenever the displayed list is not a single group.
* **Aspect: what `mark all` does when some groups have no session**
* **Alternative 1 (current choice):** check every group first, and mark nobody unless every group has a session.
* Pros: a failed command changes nothing, as for every other command.

* **Alternative 2:** mark the students whose group has a session and skip the rest.

After adding a student, `AddCommand` checks whether the student is in the displayed list. If not, for example

Each suggestion records the range of text it replaces, so accepting one leaves the rest of the command unchanged.
The `comment` command attaches free-text remarks to a student, so that a tutor can record observations
about them over a semester. `CommentCommandParser` recognises two prefixes: `c/` adds to whatever comment
the student already has, while `c-/` replaces it, and `c-/` on its own clears it. Supplying both prefixes,

rejected, leaving the student's existing comment untouched. The new comment is applied by building a
replacement immutable `Person` through `Person#withComment` and handing it to `Model#setPerson`.

The undo mechanism is facilitated by `VersionedAddressBook`. It extends `AddressBook` with a history of complete
Roster snapshots, stored internally as an `addressBookStateList` and `currentStatePointer`.
* `VersionedAddressBook#commit(String)` saves the current address book state and command name in its history.
* `VersionedAddressBook#undo()` restores the previous address book state from its history.
These operations are exposed by `Model`. `RedoCommand` checks `Model#canRedoAddressBook()` and reapplies
one state without creating another commit. `RedoCommandParser` rejects arguments, just as `UndoCommandParser` does.
`JsonSerializableAddressBook` stores the snapshot list, command names and current pointer alongside the current
roster in the same JSON file. Each snapshot uses the existing roster conversion and validation. `ModelManager`
copies this history at startup. Old files without history start at a new history boundary. Invalid histories, or
histories whose selected snapshot differs from the current roster, are discarded while retaining the current roster.
`LogicManager` captures the full pre-command roster and history, executes the command, commits data-changing
commands, and then saves the roster and history together. An unsuccessful save restores the complete pre-command
snapshot, including any redo states removed by a tentative commit. Read-only commands bypass this process.
`JsonAddressBookStorage` writes a temporary file in the same directory and replaces the destination atomically
when supported, falling back to replacement when atomic moves are unavailable. This avoids separately saving
roster data and history. History retains previous student data even after deletion or clear.
After a data-changing command such as `add`, `delete`, or `clear` executes, `LogicManager` calls
`Model#commitAddressBook()` before saving the roster and history together. Read-only and failed commands do not change the history. The default history action
is derived from `Command#requiresSave()`, while special commands such as `undo` override it. This makes new
data-changing commands undoable unless they explicitly opt out.

1. Compatibility: Roster should run on Windows, macOS, and Linux with Java 25 and the required JavaFX runtime, without requiring users to modify or compile its source code.
2. Offline operation: After installation, users should be able to manage tutorial groups, update student records, and review recorded information without an internet connection.

3. Keyboard usability: Users should be able to perform routine tasks, including adding, listing, finding and deleting students, switching tutorial groups, and recording attendance, through typed commands without requiring mouse interaction.
4. Local storage: Roster should store application data locally in a human-editable text format, without requiring a separate database server or an online account.

5. Data persistence: Following a successful save and normal application shutdown, reopening Roster should restore the saved tutorial groups, student details, and recorded attendance, participation, and assignment-completion information without alteration.

6. Input-error tolerance: Invalid commands or parameter values should not terminate the application or modify existing records. After displaying an error, Roster should remain available for the user to enter another command.

7. Error-message clarity: Input-error messages should identify the invalid or missing input and explain the expected format or accepted values, so that users can correct their commands without interpreting technical exception messages.

8. Terminology consistency: The user interface, command feedback, User Guide, and Developer Guide should use consistent terms for students, tutorial groups, sessions, attendance, participation, and assignment completion.
* **Attendance**: The record that a student was present or absent at one session.
* **Attendance percentage**: The number of sessions a student was marked present for, divided by the number of sessions the student has been marked for. Unmarked sessions are excluded.
* **Active group**: The tutorial group whose students are displayed after `list grp/GROUP` or a click in the group panel. `list` and `find` clear it.

* **Attendance strip**: The row on a student's entry that shows one cell per session of their tutorial group, in teaching-week order, such as `W5: ✓`. A green `✓` means present, a red `✗` absent and a grey `—` unmarked.
* **Comment**: A short note, of up to 200 characters, that a TA keeps about a student.
* **Displayed list**: The students currently shown in the student list. Every `INDEX`, and `all` in `mark all` and `delete all`, refers to this list.
* **Course coordinator**: The staff member in charge of a module, who collects attendance records from the TAs.
* **Index**: The one-based position of a student in the currently displayed list. It is not a property of the student: the same student's index changes when the list is filtered.
* **Mainstream OS**: Windows, Linux, Unix, or macOS
* **Matriculation number**: The unique identifier NUS assigns to each student, e.g. `A0287654J`. Roster uses it to tell apart students with the same name.
* **Participation score**: A measure of how much a student contributed during a session, recorded alongside attendance.
* **Present / Absent**: The two attendance statuses a TA can record for a student at a session.
* **Session**: A record that a tutorial group met in a particular teaching week, together with the date of that meeting. A tutorial group has at most one session per teaching week.
* **Student**: A person enrolled in one of the TA's tutorial groups. Each student belongs to exactly one tutorial group.
* **Teaching assistant (TA)**: The target user of Roster. A person who conducts tutorials for a module, usually for one to three tutorial groups of around 20 students each.
* **Teaching week**: One of the 13 weeks of instruction in an NUS semester, numbered 1 to 13. Recess week is not a teaching week.
* **Tutorial group**: A fixed set of students who meet weekly with a TA. It is identified by a group code made up of one or two letters followed by two digits, e.g. `T09`.

* **Unmarked**: The state of a student at a session for which the TA has not yet recorded present or absent. It is not stored; it is the absence of an attendance record. It is kept distinct from absent so that unprocessed records are never mistaken for absences.

**Mac users:** Ensure you have the precise JDK version prescribed [here](https://se-education.org/guides/tutorials/javaInstallationMac.html).
1. Download the latest `.jar` file from the [Roster releases page](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-F12-4/tp/releases).
1. Copy the file to an empty, writable folder you want to use as Roster's _home folder_. Roster creates its data, preferences and log files there.
1. Open a terminal, `cd` to the folder containing the JAR file, and run `java -jar "roster.jar"`.
A GUI similar to the one below should appear in a few seconds. Roster includes sample data on its first launch.
1. Type a command in the command box and press Enter to execute it. For example, type **`help`** and press Enter to open the help window.
* `add n/Alex Tan e/alex.tan@example.com m/A0123456X grp/T09` : Adds Alex Tan to `T09`.
* `session grp/T09 w/5 d/2026-09-15` : Creates the week 5 session for `T09`.
* `list grp/T09` : Shows the students in `T09` and makes it the active group.
* `mark 1 w/5 s/present` : Marks the first displayed student present for week 5.
1. Refer to the [Features](#features) section for full details of each command.
Every student belongs to exactly one tutorial group. Create a group with `init` before adding students or sessions to it.
A session records that a tutorial group met during a particular teaching week and on a particular date. A group can have at most one session per teaching week.
For each session in a student's tutorial group, their attendance is one of three states:
* **Present (`✓`)**: The student has been marked present.
* **Absent (`✗`)**: The student has been marked absent.
* **Unmarked (`—`)**: No attendance has been recorded yet. Unmarked is kept separate from absent so unfinished attendance is not mistaken for a confirmed absence.
Creating a session does not automatically mark any student. A student added after sessions have been created is also unmarked for those earlier sessions.
Roster does not yet support returning a recorded status to unmarked. You can, however, replace `present` with `absent`, or vice versa, by running `mark` again.
* `list` shows every student and clears the active group.
* `list grp/GROUP` shows one group's students and makes that group active.
* `find` searches every group and clears the active group.
* Students are listed by matriculation number in ascending order.
* `INDEX` always refers to the list currently displayed. The same student may have a different index after `list`, `list grp/GROUP`, or `find`.
* Words in `UPPER_CASE` are parameters that you must replace with your own values.
For example, replace `GROUP` in `init grp/GROUP` with a group code such as `T09`.
* Items in square brackets are optional.
For example, `list [grp/GROUP]` can be used as either `list` or `list grp/T09`.
* Prefixed parameters can be given in any order.
For example, both `session grp/T09 w/5 d/2026-09-15` and `session d/2026-09-15 grp/T09 w/5` are valid.
* A prefix marks the start of a parameter. Values containing `/` are accepted where explicitly supported, such as relationship abbreviations in names and CSV file paths.
* Unless a command states otherwise, each parameter may appear only once.
* `INDEX` must be a positive integer and always refers to the currently displayed list.
* If a command fails, Roster does not create, change, or delete any data, and the displayed list remains unchanged.
* If you are using a PDF version of this guide, take care when copying commands that span multiple lines, as spaces around line breaks may be omitted.
`grp/GROUP` | One or two letters followed by two digits, e.g. `T09` or `TG01`. Surrounding spaces are removed and letters are converted to uppercase.

`n/NAME` | 1–70 characters. Letters and their accents, spaces, hyphens, apostrophes, full stops and the relationship abbreviations `s/o`, `d/o`, `a/l`, `a/p` (in any letter case). Must begin with a letter and end with a letter, accent or full stop. Examples: `J. Tan`, `Ravi s/o Kumar`. Surrounding spaces are removed, repeated spaces become one space, and letter case is preserved.
`m/MATRIC` | `A`, followed by seven digits and one letter, e.g. `A0287654J`. Surrounding spaces are removed and letters are converted to uppercase.
`e/EMAIL` | A valid email address such as `alex.tan@example.com`. Surrounding spaces are removed and the address is converted to lowercase.
`c/COMMENT` | Text to add to a student's existing comment. 1–200 characters once surrounding spaces are removed and repeated spaces become one space.
`c-/COMMENT` | Text to replace a student's comment with. Same rules as `c/`, except that `c-/` on its own clears the comment.
`t/TAG` | One or more letters or digits, with no spaces or other characters. Repeat `t/` to give a student multiple tags.
`w/WEEK` | A whole number from `1` to `13`, without a leading zero.
`d/DATE` | A real calendar date in `YYYY-MM-DD` format.
